public_rationale: Fortune reported on June 16, 2026 that OpenAI's 2025 operating loss was $20.92 billion; this annual figure does not establish quarterly net losses through October–December 2025 [e2]. The Wall Street Journal reported on November 10, 2025 that projections shared that summer placed profitability in 2030, but did not establish a defined net-profit forecast current on February 13, 2026 [e1]. Fortune's November 12, 2025 report quoted the CFO describing hypothetical break-even under a different strategy, rather than realized profitability or a replacement forecast [e3]. These items leave both the recurring quarterly net-loss claim and the contemporaneous projection claim unresolved [e1–e3].
limitations: The packet contains no comparable series of quarterly net results through October–December 2025.
The projection reporting does not establish the latest forecast at publication or clearly define its profitability measure.
Annual operating losses, projected cash flow, and hypothetical break-even do not supply the missing quarterly net results.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI loses money every quarter and, even by its own optimistic projections, will not be profitable for years.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI is losing money every quarter; even by their own (optimistic) calculations, they won’t make a profit for years.

from_speaker: won’t make a profit for years
our_interpretation: The claim combines recurring realized losses with a description of OpenAI’s projections at publication. It does not require waiting to see whether those projections come true.
The plain reading of losing money is company-wide net losses after expenses. Cash burn, operating losses, and investors’ investment returns are distinct measures.

For the ongoing observation, use the latest completed calendar quarter before publication, October–December 2025. The target interval extends through February 13, 2026 to encompass the contemporaneous projection claim. Earlier quarterly results can establish recurrence but cannot substitute for the latest quarter.
For years means profitability was projected to remain at least several years away; the wording supplies no exact first profitable year.

The realized-loss clause supplies no accounting basis. The projection clause explicitly refers to company calculations. The single metric_scope records the unresolved basis of the realized-loss claim.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable quarterly net results establish recurring losses through the latest completed quarter, and OpenAI’s projections current at publication place company-wide profitability several years away.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable results show profitability during the claimed continuing sequence, or OpenAI’s contemporaneous projections show profitability arriving substantially sooner than several years. Evidence contradicting only one clause must be identified as such.

Loss from Operations: $20.92 billion up from $8.78 billion

evidence.explanation: The reported statements establish substantial annual operating losses. They do not provide net results for each quarter, so they cannot settle the every-quarter claim.

evidence.excerpt: OpenAI Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar said last week the company has healthy margins and could break even if it wanted to.
evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning OpenAI Chief Financial Officer
evidence.explanation: This qualifies any reading that profitability was impossible for years. It describes a hypothetical change of strategy, not actual quarterly profitability or a replacement for the company’s planned trajectory.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable company-wide quarterly net results on a consistent accounting basis through October–December 2025, plus dated company projections current on February 13, 2026 that define profitability and its expected timing.
